questions.q: How long does Gaganyaan take to go once around the Earth at its planned orbit height?
questions.do: In section 2 In orbit, set the Orbit height slider to 400 km and read the Once around tile.
questions.a: About 92 min (92.4 min). At 400 km the ship moves at about 27,600 km/h, so one lap of the Earth takes about an hour and a half.

questions.q: Compare the two real escape tests. How high did the crew module climb in each one?
questions.do: In section 1 Escape!, click Pad abort, 2018 and read Top of the arc. Then click TV-D1, 2023 and read it again.
questions.a: Pad abort: about 2.79 km. TV-D1: about 16.5 km. In TV-D1 the rocket was already about 11 km up and moving at Mach 1.2, so the capsule kept that speed and climbed much higher.

questions.q: What happens to the splashdown speed in the TV-D1 escape if one main parachute fails to open? Is the crew still safe?
questions.do: Click TV-D1, 2023. Read Splashdown speed. Then tick One main parachute fails to open and read it again.
questions.a: It rises from about 7.5 m/s to about 10.6 m/s. That is still under the 11 m/s limit, so the crew is safe. One chute is enough, and the second one is a spare for safety.

questions.q: Why does the autopilot matter when coming home? Try a hard braking burn with and without it.
questions.do: In section 3 Coming home, set Braking burn to 400 m/s. Read Hardest braking with Autopilot: roll the lift to stay under 4 g. Then change Steering to No lift (ballistic backup) and read it again.
questions.a: With the autopilot about 7.9 g. With no lift about 15.6 g, which the page marks Too steep for the crew (over 10 g). The capsule's lift lets it slow down more gently over a longer time, instead of diving straight into thick air.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian in space, and in which year? Which spacecraft did he fly on?
questions.do: Scroll to The road so far and read the first entry in the timeline.
questions.a: Rakesh Sharma, in 1984. He flew on the Soviet Soyuz T-11 under the Interkosmos programme. Gaganyaan aims to put the first Indian crew on an Indian rocket.
